title: Semi-cooperative LiDAR/inertial relative localization
description: Sharing motion information from two UAVs helps maintain relative position and velocity when compact LiDAR observations disappear.
introduction: A small UAV may produce only a few LiDAR returns, and those observations can vanish for extended intervals. This work combines intermittent detections with inertial information from both robots to maintain relative awareness through sensing gaps.

problem.heading: Keep estimating when detections stop.
paragraphs: Compact 3D LiDAR offers direct spatial observations of another UAV, but a small target can generate very few points. Orientation, scanning patterns, occlusion and clutter can interrupt detections.

A relative-state estimator must therefore bridge periods without a direct observation. A prediction based only on a simple target-motion assumption can become inaccurate when the target changes its motion.

approach.heading: Share motion, then correct with LiDAR.
paragraphs: The target UAV shares its IMU measurements and attitude estimate. The observing UAV combines those messages with its own inertial measurements and sparse onboard LiDAR detections.
A 9-DOF dual-IMU extended Kalman filter propagates relative motion during observation gaps and corrects the relative position and velocity estimate when valid detections return.

Related publications investigate adaptive LiDAR tracking and detection under extreme sparsity. Their separate experiments complement the dual-IMU study; they are not interchangeable evaluations of the same estimator.

evidence.label: Outdoor dual-IMU comparison
evidence.text: Across 13 outdoor flight segments with 3–30 m separation, the 9-DOF dual-IMU model reduced relative-position RMSE from 3.96 m to 1.43 m against a constant-velocity, non-cooperative baseline. This comparison concerns the reported outdoor dataset.

evidence.label: Intermittent observation conditions
evidence.text: Valid detections occurred in 13–41% of LiDAR scans in these experiments, with observation gaps reaching 11 seconds. These are recorded experimental conditions, rather than universal specifications of the sensor.

evidence.label: Related detection and filtering studies
evidence.text: The adaptive-filtering and severe-sparsity papers address complementary parts of UAV-to-UAV sensing. Their publication links retain their own evaluation settings and author order.
